title: Celebrity Chaos — 90s & 2000s Edition
description: A comedy-first, millennial-targeted board covering 90s/2000s one-hit wonders, classic comedy films, outrageously wild sports moments, celebrity marriages, famous splits, and the most ridiculous tabloid headlines of the era.

questions.question: This Bahamian junkanoo band became the unofficial sound of sporting events worldwide after their Grammy Award-winning 2000 track dominated stadiums from baseball diamonds to basketball arenas — despite peaking at only #40 on the US Billboard Hot 100.

This German musician's infectious 1999 debut single borrowed from a classic Pérez Prado mambo and introduced the world to a list of women's names — Monica, Erica, Rita, Tina, Sandra, Mary, and Jessica — before dominating every summer dancefloor in existence.

Three brothers from Tulsa, Oklahoma — ages 11, 14, and 16 — co-wrote this 1997 debut single entirely by themselves, topped the Billboard Hot 100 for three weeks, and then watched the music world collectively move on when their follow-up albums failed to replicate the magic.

This R&B singer's 2000 ode to a certain minimalist undergarment — from his debut album 'Unleash the Dragon' — climbed into the US Top 5 and became one of the most played and radio-edited songs of the year, inspiring untold numbers of awkward family conversations.

Few radio listeners in 1997 knew that this Australian singer's emotionally raw breakthrough hit was actually a cover of a 1995 song by the American alternative rock band Ednaswap — her smoky, stripped-down version became far more famous than the original.

In this 1996 Adam Sandler sports comedy, a former hockey player who never made it to the NHL channels his slapshot aggression into professional golf, terrorizing competitors — and an extremely annoyed Bob Barker.

In this 2001 comedy, Reese Witherspoon's bubbly sorority president shocks everyone by acing the LSAT and enrolling at Harvard Law School — where she ultimately wins a murder case by citing the rules of perming hair.

Directed by Amy Heckerling, this 1995 Beverly Hills high school comedy follows a perpetually stylish teenager who uses a computerized wardrobe selector, misquotes Hamlet, and deploys her most iconic catchphrase — 'As if!' — to navigate the politics of her wealthy world.

This 1999 raunchy teen comedy is most infamous for a scene in which a teenage boy makes an extremely poor decision with a freshly baked apple pie — a moment so notorious it defined the film's identity, inspired four sequels, and traumatized a generation of bakers.

In this 1998 Farrelly Brothers romantic comedy, Ben Stiller's character survives a horrific pre-date zipper incident, while Cameron Diaz's character later uses what she believes is 'hair gel' in one of cinema's most memorably cringe-inducing mix-ups.
questions.answer: What is There's Something About Mary?

questions.question: During their WBA heavyweight title rematch at the MGM Grand in Las Vegas on June 28, 1997, this former undisputed champion was disqualified for biting a chunk off Evander Holyfield's right ear — earning a $3 million fine and the revocation of his boxing license.

In January 1994, just weeks before the Winter Olympics, an attacker hired by this US figure skater's ex-husband Jeff Gillooly struck rival Nancy Kerrigan in the right knee with a metal baton in a Detroit arena hallway.

During a March 24, 2001 spring training game in Tucson, Arizona, this Arizona Diamondbacks Hall of Fame pitcher accidentally vaporized a mourning dove mid-flight with a near-100-mph fastball — the umpire declared the bizarre incident 'no pitch.'

On November 19, 2004, Indiana Pacers forward Ron Artest charged into the stands to fight fans after one threw a cup of soda at him — triggering the most infamous brawl in NBA history, forever nicknamed after the suburban Detroit arena where it occurred.
questions.answer: What is the Malice at the Palace?

questions.question: In 1997, this head coach of the NBA's Golden State Warriors was choked at practice by his own player Latrell Sprewell, who said he was 'tired of' the constant criticism — earning Sprewell a 68-game suspension that stood as the longest in league history until the 2004 Pacers-Pistons brawl.

This England soccer captain married Victoria 'Posh Spice' Adams at Luttrellstown Castle in Ireland on July 4, 1999, in a ceremony so lavish and publicized that tabloids quickly dubbed the couple 'Posh and Becks.'

In May 2000, this Oscar-winning actress made headlines not just for marrying actor-director Billy Bob Thornton, but for the couple's matching fashion statement: vials of each other's blood worn around their necks as jewelry.

This actor co-starred with his real-life girlfriend Reese Witherspoon in the 1999 dark teen drama 'Cruel Intentions,' then married her that same summer — the couple had two children before announcing their separation in 2006.

Just months after ending a highly publicized engagement to actor Ben Affleck, this pop star and actress quietly married Puerto Rican singer Marc Anthony in a private June 2004 ceremony attended by only about 40 guests.

At a July 1992 ceremony at her New Jersey home, this Grammy-winning R&B icon married fellow singer Bobby Brown — beginning a tumultuous union that became the subject of a 2005 VH1 reality series and ended with a 2007 divorce finalization.

When this 'Friends' actress and former wife of Brad Pitt announced their separation in January 2005 after five years of marriage, tabloids everywhere collectively lost their minds — and have barely stopped discussing it in the two decades since.

This actress — known for playing Joey Potter on Dawson's Creek — reportedly used a burner phone to secretly coordinate her exit before filing for divorce from Tom Cruise in June 2012, amid widely reported concerns about surveillance by his church.

When this pop diva's five-year marriage to Sony Music president Tommy Mottola — the man who had signed and developed her career — ended in March 1998, she described their home as a 'jail' with cameras monitoring her every move.

Fans who had watched three seasons of an MTV reality show about a young married couple were shocked in December 2005 when this 98 Degrees lead singer announced his separation from pop star and actress Jessica Simpson — their divorce was finalized in June 2006.

This Baywatch star's 1998 divorce from Mötley Crüe drummer Tommy Lee — following his conviction for spousal abuse — didn't stop the couple from dominating tabloids, as a secretly filmed honeymoon tape that leaked online in 1997 became one of the earliest major celebrity sex tape scandals.

In November 2002, while staying at the Hotel Adlon in Berlin with fans gathered below, this pop megastar shocked the world by dangling his youngest son — a then-infant nicknamed 'Blanket' — over a fourth-floor balcony railing.

In 1998, the American public's collective jaw dropped when this 22-year-old White House intern's conversations — secretly recorded by colleague Linda Tripp — were revealed in the Starr Report, detailing her relationship with President Clinton in unprecedented detail.

In a 1993 case that became one of America's most notorious tabloid stories, this Virginia woman was acquitted by reason of temporary insanity after severing her abusive husband's anatomy with a kitchen knife — later inspiring SNL sketches, a documentary, and a Netflix series.

This pop star's January 2004 Las Vegas escapade — a 55-hour marriage to Louisiana childhood friend Jason Alexander, quickly annulled after her record label described it as 'a joke taken too far' — was somehow not the most chaotic thing she did that decade.

The entire entertainment world clutched its pearls in 1994 when this former Playboy Playmate married 89-year-old Texas oil billionaire J. Howard Marshall II — a union that ended 13 months later when he died and triggered a decade-long legal battle over his estate.
